## Synthesis Overview

PR #139 is a minimal, well-scoped bug fix that adds `try/except ConfigurationError` handling around the `_load_prompt` call in `cmd_generate_handoff`, converting an unhandled exception into a clean `sys.exit(1)`. The change is accompanied by a targeted unit test. All three models agree the fix is correct, safe, and ready to merge with no security, performance, or correctness concerns. The only point of divergence is a stylistic finding — import placement — which two of the three models flagged. Agreement among models is high overall.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

No unanimous findings. All three models agreed on the overall clean state of the PR (no critical, no security, no correctness issues).

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

```
[M-W-01] Import placed inside function body rather than at module level
Severity: Warning
Category: Style
File: src/tools/story_assembler.py
Lines: 262
Detail: The new import `from domain.exceptions import ConfigurationError` is placed
  inside the body of `cmd_generate_handoff` rather than at module level. Both Claude
  and Gemini flagged this as a violation of the project convention specifying imports
  at module level, not inside functions or loops. Claude additionally noted that
  this is consistent with two pre-existing inline imports already present in the
  same file (`_load_prompt` uses `from infrastructure.prompts.prompt_loader import
  PromptLoader`; `_call_llm` uses `from src.tools._llm import generate_text`),
  making the PR internally consistent with the file's established pattern —
  even though that pattern itself diverges from the project-wide convention.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✗  Gemini ✓
Dissenting view: GPT found no findings at all. It reviewed the same file and lines
  without flagging the import placement. This is likely a genuine difference in
  review depth rather than a substantive disagreement — GPT acknowledged the fix
  was consistent with surrounding patterns without analysing import placement
  specifically.
Suggestion: Move `from domain.exceptions import ConfigurationError` to the module-level
  import block. Because two other inline imports in the same file carry the same
  issue, a follow-up cleanup pass addressing all three would be the most coherent
  approach. If the inline pattern is intentional (lazy-loading or circular-import
  avoidance), document the reason with a comment.
```
